title: Modular Architecture for High-Performance and Low Overhead Data Transfers
problem: Traditional file transfer tools suffer from resource underutilization and instability due to fixed configurations or monolithic optimization methods; adapting to changing network/system conditions is difficult.
motivation: Large-scale scientific data transfers across geographically dispersed locations require both speed and adaptability; static tuning cannot handle dynamic network conditions.
method: AutoMDT breaks data transfer into three separate, independently-optimizable stages—reading, network transfer, and writing—and uses machine learning (specifically reinforcement learning, where an agent learns by trying actions and getting rewarded for good results) to find the optimal number of simultaneous operations for each stage. The learning method, called PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization), is designed to be stable and efficient. To avoid slowing production networks, the system trains this learning offline using a lightweight simulator that accurately mimics real network and system behavior—this training takes about 45 minutes.
key_novelty: AutoMDT is the first modular data-transfer framework using reinforcement learning (PPO) to automatically optimize how many operations run in parallel at each stage, learning this from a lightweight network simulator offline.
contributions: Modular architecture decoupling I/O and network tasks
PPO agent for adaptive concurrency optimization
Lightweight network-system simulator for offline training
limitations: Abstract-only; lacks details on specific baseline comparisons, dataset sizes, or network topologies tested
